name: Atlantoaxial Rotatory Subluxation
definition: Rotational malalignment of C1 relative to C2, most often seen in children after minor trauma, infection or surgery and presenting with painful torticollis.

redFlags.item: Fever with deep neck infection concern

investigations.principle: CT can define rotational alignment; MRI is selected for neurological, ligamentous or infection concern.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, inflammatory, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Forceful manipulation should be avoided; persistent fixed cases may need traction or surgical treatment.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Greeva-stambha phenotype may be documented after modern instability assessment.

patientEducation.summary: Rotational malalignment of C1 relative to C2, most often seen in children after minor trauma, infection or surgery and presenting with painful torticollis.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
